worked_solution:
To find the Cartesian equation of the hyperbola, we need to eliminate the parameter $t.$ We can do this using the secant–tangent identity.

- Isolating the $\operatorname{tan}⁡t$ term in the $x$-equation and squaring, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =3\sqrt{5}\,\operatorname{tan}⁡t \\ \frac{x}{3\sqrt{5}} & =\operatorname{tan}⁡t \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{(3\sqrt{5})^{2}} & ={tan}^{2}⁡t \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{45} & ={tan}^{2}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

- Isolating the $\operatorname{sec}⁡t$ term in the $y$-equation and squaring, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =2\sqrt{6}\,\operatorname{sec}⁡t \\ \frac{y}{2\sqrt{6}} & =\operatorname{sec}⁡t \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{(2\sqrt{6})^{2}} & ={sec}^{2}⁡t \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{24} & ={sec}^{2}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the two equations into the identity ${tan}^{2}⁡t+1={sec}^{2}⁡t$ and rearranging, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{tan}^{2}⁡t+1 & ={sec}^{2}⁡t \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{45}+1 & =\frac{{y}^{2}}{24} \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{24}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{45} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
